chunks: Everything that was in it from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, I have narrated from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father; the author's immediate transmitter in this chain
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلْوَانَ: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlwān, a transmitter in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.الْهَيْثَمِ بْنِ أَبِي مَسْرُوقٍ النَّهْ: al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, a transmitter in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; a formal hadith-transmission expression
key_terms.سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, a transmitter in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ: ʿAmr ibn Khālid, the narrator to whom this transmission chain leads

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to ʿAmr ibn Khālid in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from ʿAmr ibn Khālid in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. It is a technical chain statement used to document transmission authority and preserve hadith provenance.
